t: Cells in a Range on an Excel Sheet — Simple Enumeration
o: We must expand a range like "K1:L2" into every cell string between the two corners, ordered column-major (columns outer loop, rows inner loop). Since s always has length 5, s[0]/s[3] are the column letters and s[1]/s[4] are the row digits. In example 1, columns K..L and rows 1..2 give K1,K2,L1,L2; in example 2, columns A..F with row 1 give A1..F1. Constraints guarantee single-letter columns and single-digit rows, so direct character arithmetic suffices.
k: Parse fixed positions: s[0], s[1] are the top-left corner, s[3], s[4] the bottom-right.

a.i: Convert column letters to their character codes and row digits to integers, then run an outer loop over columns and inner loop over rows, rebuilding each cell string. This naturally produces the required column-major order.
s: Loop col from c1 to c2, loop row from r1 to r2.
Append chr(col)+str(row) to the answer list.
a.t: O(1) — at most 26*9 cells are generated.

w: This is a pure implementation warm-up. Pitfalls: forgetting the column-major ordering, or off-by-one on inclusive bounds. Follow-ups usually ask for multi-letter columns (Excel sheet column title conversion), which requires base-26 arithmetic instead.
